findings.evidence: The materializer copies deps/telemetry/.hex and computes its new hash without comparing it to the reviewed acquisition receipt or frozen inventory. Shipped telemetry bytes and archive checksums are verified, but .hex is not archive-shipped and is outside those checks. The current .hex hash passes an independent read-only check; the script itself does not enforce that identity.
findings.required_change: Before the first preserve call, require a PASS acquisition receipt and compare the installed .hex hash to its reviewed installed_hex_sha256 or the independently frozen inventory value. Fail before writing if it differs.
findings.title: Verify installed telemetry .hex before any destination writes

findings.evidence: install_tools validates existing files under MIX_HOME and source/archive symlinks, but HEX_HOME is only mkdir(exist_ok=True). An existing candidate .hex directory symlink is accepted and supplied to the VM; stale/unlisted .hex contents are neither rejected nor frozen. Existing unlisted empty MIX_HOME directories are also accepted. The collector lacks the materializer complete-destination prevalidation for its separately owned candidate tool root.
findings.required_change: Before any tool destination writes, reject symlinked target/HEX_HOME/ancestors and stale or unlisted files/directories in the complete owned tool root. Bind HEX_HOME to its intended real owned root and include its inventory in before/after receipts. Preserve mismatching existing bytes and stop rather than deleting them.
findings.title: Validate the complete owned Hex/tool destination inventory before copying

findings.evidence: After process.wait returns an actual exit, outer calls protected(), source/build scanning and JSON parsing before creating the final receipt. protected validates frozen inputs while reading them; a changed/missing input raises immediately. That failure path preserves the raw log but loses the final receipt containing the actual exit and distinct identity error. The wrapper primary/post separation is repaired, but the outer collector can still replace the command outcome with a post-collection exception.
findings.required_change: Capture the actual process exit/timing immediately. Attempt each post collection independently, retain its raw data or explicit failure, and always write a final receipt containing primary exit plus separate post-identity/collection errors. Fail qualification on any missing/mismatching post evidence while preserving the driver failure.
findings.title: Always preserve the actual command exit and post-identity failures

findings.evidence: The profiler hashes each selected tool entry point and follows ldd dependencies only for ELF files. It does not follow shell/Tcl scripts, executable wrapper targets, interpreter/package inputs, or non-ELF launcher dependencies. Installed expect layouts have an ELF bin/unbuffer and a separate bin/.unbuffer-wrapped script that executes tclsh and package require Expect. The collector launches unbuffer, but none of that hidden script/interpreter/package closure is added by this profiler. The profiler does not launch unbuffer, so its Python /proc maps cannot supply that missing closure. ELF linkage of the wrapper alone does not include executables/scripts it later launches.
findings.required_change: Freeze and validate the actual selected unbuffer wrapper target, Tcl interpreter and required Expect/Tcl package inputs, and equivalent transitive inputs for the other selected script/wrapper launchers and compiler tools. Keep file-identity claims separate from ABI/lifetime qualification.
findings.title: Native profiler omits transitive launcher/interpreter inputs

findings.evidence: The only initial evidence-preservation guard checks name.json. All sidecar JSON writes use write_text. A failed attempt before the final name.json can leave environment/source/tool/inner receipts; retrying that name overwrites those sidecars before the later exclusive log open fails. The raw log guard therefore does not protect the already written partial receipts.
findings.required_change: Reserve every output name before any mutation or use exclusive creation for all evidence files. Reject a reused name if any corresponding log/sidecar/final receipt exists, including incomplete attempts. Never replace prior failure evidence.
findings.title: Partial failure receipts can be overwritten on a same-name retry
